tasks.title: Security basics
tasks.description: Fail fast without a real SECRET_KEY, restrict CORS, and stop strangers from registering on the public URL.
tasks.details:
- backend/utils/security.py: remove the default `"your-secret-key-change-in-production-please"`. If SECRET_KEY is unset
  or shorter than 32 chars, raise at import time with a clear message. (The default is public on GitHub, so anyone could forge login tokens.)
- backend/main.py: replace `allow_origins=["*"]` with `os.getenv("ALLOWED_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:5173").split(",")`.
  In production the frontend is same-origin (nginx /api), so CORS barely matters, but `*` with credentials is wrong.
- Registration lock: env `ALLOW_REGISTRATION` (default "true"). In routers/auth.py register endpoint, return 403
  "Registration is closed" when it is "false". After both people have accounts (task 19), set it to false on the VPS.
- Check token lifetime in utils/security.py: use 30 days for this personal app so nobody gets logged out weekly
  (phones keep the PWA open for weeks); keep it configurable via ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS.
- Add backend/tests/test_security.py using FastAPI TestClient.
tasks.testStrategy:

tasks.title: Adopt Alembic migrations
tasks.description: Replace Base.metadata.create_all with Alembic so existing tables can be changed safely (create_all never alters a table).
tasks.details:
- `pip install alembic` is already in requirements. In backend/: `alembic init alembic`.
- alembic/env.py: `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv()`; set `config.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", os.environ["DATABASE_URL"])`;
  `from database import Base; import models; target_metadata = Base.metadata`.
- Exclude the food tables, which food_data/schema.sql owns: add `include_object` that returns False for tables
  `foods` and `food_portions` (and anything with `info={"managed_by": "food_data"}`). Pass it to context.configure.
- Baseline: on an EMPTY local db run `alembic revision --autogenerate -m "baseline"`, review the file (it must create the
  existing tables only), `alembic upgrade head`.
- Existing databases that already have the tables (e.g. an old VPS install): `alembic stamp head` instead of upgrade.
  Write this in backend/README.md.
- Remove `Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)` from main.py startup. scripts/vps/deploy.sh already runs
  `alembic upgrade head` once backend/alembic.ini exists.
tasks.testStrategy:
Drop and recreate the local db, run `alembic upgrade head`, start uvicorn, register a user and log a food via /docs.
`alembic check` (or `alembic revision --autogenerate` producing an empty migration) shows models and db agree.

tasks.title: Local food database (schema, importers, search, barcode)
tasks.description: Free, self-hosted food data in Postgres: USDA Foundation + SR Legacy, Health Canada CNF, Open Food Facts (Canada/US), with ranked search and barcode lookup.
tasks.details:
Built in backend/food_data/:
- schema.sql: tables `foods` (values per 100 g, source, barcode as EAN-13, popularity, quality ok|suspect,
  created_by_user for custom foods, generated search_text/search_vec) and `food_portions` (label, grams);
  function `search_foods(q, lim, for_user)` - two-stage: up to 400 prefix-match candidates (generic + custom first, then
  most-scanned), trigram fallback for typos when too few, then ranking. ~30 ms on 500k rows.
- common.py: connection (DATABASE_URL or backend/.env), barcode normalisation (UPC-A -> EAN-13), sanity checks
  (reject >902 kcal/100 g, macros >105 g; flag Atwater mismatch as suspect), COPY-based upsert keyed on (source, source_id).
- import_usda.py (folder or zip; Foundation energy falls back to Atwater 2047/2048, then 4/4/9 maths),
  import_cnf.py (2015 and 2026 layouts, columns matched loosely, nutrients by code then name, --inspect),
  import_off.py (DuckDB streams the 9 GB CSV, keeps --countries canada,united-states with energy data).
- service.py: search_foods(db, q, limit, user_id), get_food(db, id), lookup_barcode(db, code, user_id)
  (local first, else one live OFF API call per real scan, cached into foods). Each food comes with portions,
  "100 g" always first.
- tests/: fixtures shaped like the real downloads; 10 tests.
Licences/attribution to show in the app: USDA FoodData Central (public domain), "Canadian Nutrient File, Health Canada"
(Open Government Licence - Canada), "Open Food Facts" (ODbL).

tasks.title: Custom foods
tasks.description: Users can create, edit and delete their own private foods, including from a failed barcode scan and as a corrected copy of a bad entry.
tasks.details:
routers/food.py:
- POST /food/custom {name, brand?, barcode?, basis: "100g" | "serving", serving_g?, serving_label?, kcal, protein, carbs, fat,
  fiber?, sugar?, sodium_mg?}. If basis == "serving", convert to per-100 g using serving_g (required then). Insert into foods with
  source='custom', source_id=f"u{user_id}-{uuid4().hex[:12]}", created_by_user=user_id, barcode normalised with
  food_data.common.normalize_barcode, plus a portion row for the serving.
- PUT /food/custom/{id}, DELETE /food/custom/{id}: owner only (404 otherwise). Deleting sets food_entries.food_id NULL via FK.
- POST /food/{id}/copy -> creates a custom copy the user can then edit ("this label is wrong" flow).
- lookup_barcode already prefers the user's own custom food for a barcode, so a fixed copy wins next scan.

tasks.title: Barcode scanner that works on iPhone and Android
tasks.description: Replace quagga with the BarcodeDetector API plus the barcode-detector (ZXing WebAssembly) polyfill; misses lead to 'add this food'.
tasks.details:
- `npm rm quagga && npm i barcode-detector` (v3.x). iPhone Safari has no native BarcodeDetector, so use the package's
  ponyfill: `import { BarcodeDetector, prepareZXingModule } from "barcode-detector/ponyfill"`, only when
  `!("BarcodeDetector" in window)`; otherwise use the native one.
- Self-host the .wasm (the package fetches it from jsDelivr by default, which breaks offline/PWA): import
  `zxing_reader.wasm?url` from node_modules/zxing-wasm/dist/reader/ and pass it via prepareZXingModule({overrides: {locateFile}}).
  Check the package README for the exact current path before coding.
- components/BarcodeScanner.jsx: getUserMedia({video: {facingMode: {ideal: "environment"}}}); <video playsInline muted autoPlay>
  (playsInline is required on iOS); detect every ~150 ms with formats ["ean_13","ean_8","upc_a","upc_e"]; require the same code
  twice in a row before accepting; vibrate(50) if available; torch toggle when track.getCapabilities().torch; always stop tracks on close.
- On a code: foodAPI.byBarcode(code) -> PortionPicker. On 404: "Not found - add it" opens the custom food form with the barcode filled.
- Manual fallback: a "type the number" field.
- Camera needs HTTPS (localhost is fine). To test on a phone before task 17, use `npm i -D @vitejs/plugin-basic-ssl` +
  `vite --host` and accept the warning, or test on the deployed VPS.

floor (never below 1200 kcal female / 1500 male); protein default ~1.8 g/kg bodyweight. Add vitest (`npm i -D vitest`,
script "test": "vitest run") with tests for the formula. Onboarding saves targets to the user profile (PUT /users/me or existing
endpoint); Profile page lets the user override calories and macros manually.
tasks.testStrategy: `npm test`: 30 y, 165 cm, 60 kg, female, moderate -> BMR 1320.25, TDEE ~2046. Manual: edit targets in Profile, Today screen updates.

tasks.title: Weight log and trend
tasks.description: Log weight quickly and see a smoothed trend.
tasks.details:
Check the existing WeightLog model/endpoints (grep "weight" in routers/users.py and dashboard.py) and the Progress page.
Add: quick "log weight" on Progress (and optionally Today), kg/lb toggle stored on the profile, chart of daily weights
with a 7-day moving average line (Recharts), last 30/90 days. One entry per day (logging again replaces that day's value).
tasks.testStrategy: Log 5 weights on different days; chart shows points and the average line; logging twice on one day keeps one value.

tasks.title: Make it an installable PWA
tasks.description: Manifest, icons, service worker and iOS tags so it installs from the browser and opens full-screen.
tasks.details:
- `npm i -D vite-plugin-pwa` (v1.x supports Vite 5). vite.config.js: VitePWA({ registerType: "autoUpdate",
  manifest: { name: "FitTrack+", short_name: "FitTrack", start_url: "/", scope: "/", display: "standalone",
  background_color: "#ffffff", theme_color: "#F0A7D9", icons: [192, 512, and a 512 maskable] },
  workbox: { navigateFallback: "/index.html", navigateFallbackDenylist: [/^\/api\//],
  runtimeCaching: [{ urlPattern: /^\/api\//, handler: "NetworkOnly" }] } }).
  Never cache API responses: diaries must always be fresh.
- Icons: frontend/public/icons/ (192, 512, maskable-512, apple-touch-icon 180x180). Generate from one square logo
  (e.g. `npx @vite-pwa/assets-generator`).
- frontend/index.html: <meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes">, apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style,
  <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/icons/apple-touch-icon.png">, viewport with viewport-fit=cover; use
  env(safe-area-inset-bottom) padding for the bottom nav.
- An "Install the app" page/modal: iPhone = Safari > Share > Add to Home Screen; Android = Chrome menu > Install app.
  Show it once after first login if not running standalone (matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)')).
- nginx already serves sw.js and the manifest with no-cache (scripts/vps/setup_server.sh).
tasks.testStrategy:
`npm run build` emits dist/sw.js and dist/manifest.webmanifest. Chrome devtools > Application > Manifest shows no errors and
"installable". After deploy (task 17), installing on both phones opens full-screen with the icon, and the scanner still works.

tasks.title: Server setup, first deploy, real food data
tasks.description: Put the app on the VPS with HTTPS and load the real food databases.
tasks.details: All scripts are idempotent; read their header comments first.
tasks.testStrategy:
https://<domain> loads with a valid certificate; /api/health returns 200; the 5 searches in PRD success criterion 1 return sensible
top-3 results in under 300 ms (check the browser Network tab).

subtasks.title: DNS and server setup
subtasks.description: Point the domain at the VPS and run setup_server.sh.
subtasks.details:
Create a DNS A record (e.g. fit.yourdomain.com) -> VPS IP; wait until `dig +short fit.yourdomain.com` shows it.
On the VPS: `sudo DOMAIN=fit.yourdomain.com EMAIL=you@example.com bash scripts/vps/setup_server.sh` (download the script with
curl first if the repo isn't cloned yet; see its header). It installs Postgres/nginx/certbot/Node 22, creates the fittrack user,
database and backend/.env with random secrets, systemd unit fittrack-backend, nginx site, firewall, HTTPS and the nightly backup cron.
If an OLD FitTrack+ install exists at /var/www/fittrack-plus: first `sudo -u postgres pg_dump -Fc <olddb> > ~/old.dump`.
subtasks.testStrategy: `systemctl status fittrack-backend nginx postgresql` all active (backend may fail until 17.3); `curl -I https://<domain>` -> 200.

subtasks.title: Existing data (only if an old install had real data)
subtasks.description: Bring the old database under Alembic.
subtasks.details:
If the old database has data worth keeping: point DATABASE_URL at it, run `alembic stamp <baseline revision>` then
`alembic upgrade head`. If it only has test data, skip and use the fresh database.
subtasks.testStrategy: `alembic current` on the VPS shows head.

subtasks.title: First deploy
subtasks.details:
`sudo bash /var/www/fittrack-plus/scripts/vps/deploy.sh` - pulls main, installs Python deps, runs migrations and the food schema,
builds the frontend with VITE_API_URL=/api, restarts the API and checks /health.
subtasks.testStrategy: Script ends with 'Deployed <sha>. API healthy.'; registering a user on https://<domain> works.

subtasks.title: Download and import food data
subtasks.description: Real USDA, CNF and Open Food Facts data.
subtasks.details:
`sudo -u fittrack bash /var/www/fittrack-plus/scripts/food/download_food_data.sh` (~1.5 GB to /var/lib/fittrack/fooddata).
Then FIRST `cd /var/www/fittrack-plus/backend && sudo -u fittrack venv/bin/python -m food_data.import_cnf /var/lib/fittrack/fooddata/cnf --inspect`
- the CNF 2026 layout was not verifiable when the importer was written; if it reports missing columns, fix the candidate lists
in import_cnf.py locally, test, push, deploy.
Then `sudo -u fittrack bash /var/www/fittrack-plus/scripts/food/import_food_data.sh` (10-30 min). If the VPS has <2 GB RAM add
`--memory-limit 512MB`. If USDA has published a newer Foundation release, set USDA_FOUNDATION_URL (see the download script).
subtasks.testStrategy: The summary prints counts for usda_foundation, usda_sr, cnf, off (expect off in the hundreds of thousands) and sensible top results.

subtasks.title: Speed and sanity check
subtasks.description: Measure search speed on the real data.
subtasks.details:
In the app: search banana, chicken breast, greek yogurt, kraft dinner, shreddies. If any search takes >300 ms server-side
(check `journalctl -u fittrack-backend` timing or EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT * FROM search_foods('greek yog', 20)), log it on this task
and consider: `VACUUM ANALYZE foods;`, raising work_mem, or --min-scans 1 on the OFF import to drop never-scanned products.
subtasks.testStrategy: All five searches under 300 ms; results recorded in the task log.

tasks.title: Backups and a restore drill
tasks.description: Prove the nightly backup works and can be restored.
tasks.details:
- The morning after setup: `ls -lh /var/backups/fittrack` shows a .dump; `tail /var/log/fittrack-backup.log` shows no errors.
- Restore drill without touching production: `sudo -u postgres createdb fittrack_restore_test &&
  sudo -u postgres pg_restore -d fittrack_restore_test /var/backups/fittrack/<latest>.dump`, compare
  `SELECT count(*) FROM users; ... food_entries;` with production, then `dropdb fittrack_restore_test`.
- Off-server copy from your computer: `scp you@vps:/var/backups/fittrack/<latest>.dump .` (automate later: parking lot).
- scripts/vps/restore_db.sh is the real (destructive) restore; don't run it as part of the drill.
tasks.testStrategy: Row counts in the restored test db match production; the drill is logged on this task with the date.

tasks.title: Phone install and 7-day trial
tasks.description: Both people install it, log for a week, and the top friction gets fixed.
tasks.details:
- Install on both phones (task 16 instructions); register both accounts; then set ALLOW_REGISTRATION=false in backend/.env on the VPS
  and `sudo systemctl restart fittrack-backend`.
- Barcode test: 10 random packaged foods from the kitchen; record found/missed. Add misses as custom foods (timed: < 1 min each).
- Log every meal for 7 days. Keep a friction list in .taskmaster/docs/parking-lot.md (date, what was annoying, how often).
- At the end: promote the top 3 friction items to new tasks (tasks.py add) and fix them; mark the PRD success criteria in the
  decision log.
tasks.testStrategy:
PRD success criteria 1-5 checked off in the decision log with dates. Both users have 7 consecutive days with entries:
`SELECT user_id, count(DISTINCT entry_date) FROM food_entries WHERE entry_date > now() - interval '8 days' GROUP BY 1;` -> 7 each.
